title: The coast from the air — "Nha Trang area?"
description: An aerial over a coastal port, with an out-of-focus mechanical fitting of the aircraft in the left foreground: a ship at a T-pier with a road running to the shore, barge moorings at right, cleared lots and scrub inland, and across the water a rounded, forested island closing the bay. "I think this is the coast of Vietnam, Nha Trang area?"
researchNotes: Larry's caption of 2026-09-05 (giscus-vn-0090-c18308127.json) ends in a question mark, so no place is entered. The survey independently proposed Nha Trang or Cam Ranh from the island profile, and noted that an exposed rotor head in the foreground points to a light observation helicopter rather than a Huey — which would be a different aircraft from Rosethorn 007 and a different kind of flight. Both are machine hypotheses. What the fitting in the foreground is (a rotor head, a gun mount, something else) is not settled from the scan, so the title and description say only that the picture was taken from the air (2026-09-14; they had said helicopter and rotor mast). Nha Trang was Larry's first station in Vietnam (VN-0021, VN-0022), which makes his guess plausible without making it more.
